"MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PART 1 OF 4 — CORE GAME DESIGN, LANDSCAPE CONFIGURATION, CONTROLS, MOVEMENT AND COMBAT

You are developing a complete 2D side-scrolling action roguelike game inspired by the Naruto universe.

The gameplay should take strong mechanical inspiration from Dead Cells: responsive movement, challenging combat, interconnected rooms, branching routes, precise dodging, parrying, combos, aerial combat, powerful enemies, boss encounters, and a progression system built around collecting abilities and improving builds.

This must feel like a real action roguelike, not a generic RPG, not a turn-based game, not an arena fighter, and not a basic platformer with a few abilities.

The game must be designed specifically for mobile devices.

---

1. ABSOLUTE SCREEN ORIENTATION REQUIREMENTS

THIS SECTION HAS THE HIGHEST PRIORITY. DO NOT IGNORE IT.

The entire game must use a horizontal LANDSCAPE orientation.

- Lock the project orientation to landscape.
- Never generate portrait gameplay.
- Never generate portrait menus.
- Never rotate the camera into portrait mode.
- Never place the main gameplay interface vertically.
- Never use a default portrait mobile-game template.
- Every gameplay screen, menu, inventory, customization screen, reward screen, and pause menu must be designed horizontally.

If the development environment has a default portrait configuration, override it before creating the game.

1.1 Screen proportions

Use these reference resolutions:

- Target display resolution: 1920 × 1080.
- Internal pixel-art rendering resolution: 480 × 270.
- Logical UI coordinate system: 960 × 540.
- Aspect ratio: 16:9.

The game must also support wider mobile displays, including 18:9, 19.5:9, and 20:9.

For wider screens:

- Expand the visible environment horizontally.
- Keep the central gameplay composition consistent.
- Do not stretch characters, sprites, backgrounds, or UI.
- Do not distort the aspect ratio.
- Keep buttons inside safe screen boundaries.

1.2 Camera

Use a 2D side-view camera.

The player should normally remain around 35–45% of the screen width, leaving enough visible space ahead to anticipate enemies and obstacles.

Camera behavior:

- Smooth horizontal follow.
- Slight vertical adjustment when jumping or falling.
- Do not make the camera rotate.
- Do not use a top-down camera.
- Do not use an isometric camera.
- Keep bosses and important enemies visible whenever possible.
- Avoid excessive camera shake.
- Use controlled camera movement during boss attacks and major events.

The environment must scroll horizontally as the player moves through the level.

1.3 Screen layout

All interface elements must be arranged for horizontal gameplay.

Top-left:

- Health bar.
- Chakra bar.
- Stamina bar.
- Player level.
- Small status effects.

Top-center:

- Current chapter.
- Current room name.
- Current objective.

Top-right:

- Currency.
- Map button.
- Pause button.
- Optional progression indicators.

Bottom-left:

- Virtual movement joystick.

Bottom-right:

- Combat buttons.
- Skill buttons.
- Jump.
- Dash.
- Block/Parry.

The center of the screen must remain as clear as possible so the player can see the character, enemies, attacks, and environment.

1.4 Character proportions

Characters must be designed as side-view pixel-art sprites.

Suggested sprite dimensions:

Character type| Approximate sprite size
Player| 32 × 48 px
Small enemy| 32 × 40 px
Standard enemy| 40 × 48 px
Elite enemy| 48 × 64 px
Mini-boss| 80–112 px
Standard boss| 128–192 px
Bijuu| 256 × 192 px or larger

These are reference sizes, not mandatory limits.

Characters must be readable at the internal rendering resolution.

1.5 Required orientation validation

Before implementing the rest of the game, verify:

1. The project is locked to landscape.
2. The camera is side-view.
3. The joystick is positioned on the left.
4. Combat buttons are positioned on the right.
5. The environment scrolls horizontally.
6. All menus are landscape.
7. The HUD is horizontal.
8. No default portrait UI elements remain.

Do not proceed with a portrait-based prototype.

---

2. GAMEPLAY IDENTITY

The main gameplay loop must be:

1. Enter a mission.
2. Explore interconnected rooms.
3. Fight enemies.
4. Collect rewards.
5. Choose branching paths.
6. Improve the current run.
7. Encounter stronger enemies.
8. Defeat bosses.
9. Unlock permanent progression.
10. Continue toward the final objective or die and restart.

The game should reward skill, timing, positioning, and strategic ability combinations.

Combat must be fast, responsive, and challenging.

Enemies must be able to punish careless attacks.

The player must be able to:

- Move left and right.
- Jump.
- Double jump when unlocked.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Perform light attacks.
- Perform heavy attacks.
- Perform aerial attacks.
- Use ninja tools.
- Use chakra abilities.
- Switch between equipped skills.
- Chain attacks into combos.
- Cancel certain animations into defensive actions.

Every action must have a clear animation and gameplay purpose.

---

3. MOBILE CONTROL SYSTEM

The controls must be designed specifically for touchscreen devices.

The interface must remain on the lower portions of the landscape screen without covering important gameplay information.

All buttons must have:

- Clear visual states.
- Press animations.
- Responsive input.
- Configurable opacity.
- Adjustable size.
- Adjustable position.
- Optional vibration feedback.
- Consistent spacing.

Players must be able to customize the control layout.

3.1 Virtual joystick

Position: bottom-left.

Reference configuration:

- Diameter: 104 logical UI units.
- Left margin: 80 units.
- Bottom margin: 90 units.

The joystick must support:

- Left movement.
- Right movement.
- Neutral position.
- Optional directional input for aerial movement.

Use a floating or fixed joystick, depending on which implementation is more reliable.

3.2 Main attack button

Position: bottom-right.

Reference configuration:

- Diameter: 68 units.
- Right margin: 85 units.
- Bottom margin: 90 units.

Function: Light Attack.

Repeated presses must create a combo.

3.3 Heavy attack button

Position: immediately left of the main attack button.

Reference diameter: 64 units.

Function: Heavy Attack.

Heavy attacks must be slower and more powerful than light attacks.

3.4 Jump button

Position: above the main attack button.

Reference diameter: 66 units.

Function: Jump.

Allow the player to jump while moving.

3.5 Dash button

Position: below the jump button.

Reference diameter: 62 units.

Function: Dash.

The dash must follow the player's directional input.

3.6 Block and Parry button

Position: above the heavy attack button.

Reference diameter: 68 units.

This is one defensive button with two different functions:

- Holding the button activates Block.
- Pressing it with precise timing activates Parry.

Do not create separate block and parry buttons.

3.7 Skill buttons

Provide two primary skill buttons.

- Skill 1: approximately 60 units.
- Skill 2: approximately 60 units.

They must be positioned around the right-side combat controls without overlapping the main attack button.

3.8 Chakra button

Reference diameter: 56 units.

Use this button for a configured chakra-related action, such as chakra charging or a special ability activation, depending on the selected build.

3.9 Button customization

Allow players to:

- Increase button size up to 140%.
- Decrease button size down to 70%.
- Move buttons within safe screen boundaries.
- Change button opacity.
- Restore default positions.

Save control settings permanently.

---

4. MOVEMENT SYSTEM

Movement must feel similar in responsiveness to a polished action platformer.

Use these initial reference values:

Property| Base value
Horizontal movement speed| 220 px/s
Acceleration| 1800 px/s²
Air control| 85%
Gravity| 1200 px/s²
Jump force| 480
Maximum falling speed| 650

These values should be adjustable during balancing.

4.1 Ground movement

- Smooth acceleration.
- Responsive stopping.
- No excessive sliding.
- No delayed directional input.
- Character animation must match movement speed.

4.2 Jumping

The player must have a responsive jump.

Requirements:

- Variable jump height if the jump button is held.
- Short input buffering.
- Coyote time of approximately 0.10 seconds.
- Proper landing animations.
- Different aerial attack animations.

4.3 Advanced movement

Additional movement abilities may be unlocked through progression:

- Double Jump.
- Wall Jump.
- Wall Slide.
- Air Dash.
- Chakra-enhanced movement.
- Temporary movement buffs.

These abilities must not all be available automatically at the beginning.

4.4 Environmental interaction

The player must be able to:

- Stand on platforms.
- Fall through designated platforms.
- Jump between different heights.
- Climb designated passages.
- Enter doors and room transitions.
- Interact with objects.
- Activate checkpoints.
- Discover hidden passages.

Every platform and passage must be physically reachable.

Do not generate impossible jumps or inaccessible rewards.

---

5. DASH SYSTEM

Dash is a core defensive and mobility mechanic.

Initial configuration:

Property| Value
Duration| 0.30 seconds
Distance| Approximately 105 px
Cooldown| 0.70 seconds
Invulnerability duration| 0.16 seconds

Requirements:

- Dash horizontally by default.
- Allow diagonal dash when directional input is provided.
- Support ground dash.
- Support air dash when unlocked or configured.
- Create a brief visual afterimage.
- Prevent the player from being permanently invulnerable.
- Use a clear cooldown indicator.

The dash may cancel certain attack recovery animations, but it must not cancel every action without restrictions.

Some boss attacks must require correct timing rather than simply allowing the player to dash continuously.

---

6. BLOCK AND PARRY SYSTEM

Block and Parry are essential mechanics.

They must be implemented as two outcomes of the same defensive button.

6.1 Block

Holding the defensive button activates Block.

Initial values:

- Reduce incoming damage by 70%.
- Maximum stamina: 100.
- Blocking consumes 12 stamina per second.
- Stamina regeneration: 25 per second when not blocking.

Additional rules:

- Blocking reduces knockback.
- Blocking does not eliminate all damage.
- Certain powerful attacks break through guard.
- Some attacks cause additional stamina loss.
- The player cannot block indefinitely.

If stamina reaches zero, the player enters a short guard-break state.

6.2 Parry

A Parry happens when the defensive button is pressed at the correct moment.

Initial perfect-parry window:

- 0.12 seconds.

A successful Parry must:

1. Negate an eligible incoming attack.
2. Play a unique defensive animation.
3. Produce a clear visual effect.
4. Play a distinct sound effect.
5. Briefly stun the attacker.
6. Restore 15 stamina.
7. Restore 5 chakra.

Parry timing must be skill-based.

Do not allow players to hold the button and automatically parry everything.

6.3 Failed Parry

If the player presses the defensive button too early or too late:

- It may become a normal Block if the button remains held.
- Normal stamina requirements still apply.
- The player must not receive the benefits of a successful Parry.

6.4 Attack compatibility

Not every attack must be parryable.

Use these rules:

- Light attacks can generally be blocked.
- Some light attacks may be parried, depending on the enemy.
- Heavy attacks can be parried with precise timing when explicitly designed to allow it.
- Certain large attacks must be avoided with movement or Dash.
- Environmental attacks cannot automatically be parried.
- Ultimate attacks must have clear visual telegraphs.

Enemies must communicate their attack type through animation and visual effects.

A parryable attack should have a recognizable timing cue.

---

7. COMBAT SYSTEM

Combat must be based on responsive action-game mechanics.

Every attack must have:

- Startup frames.
- Active frames.
- Recovery frames.
- Hitbox.
- Damage.
- Knockback.
- Hitstun.
- Animation.
- Sound effect.
- Visual effect.

Avoid attacks that simply subtract health without meaningful interaction.

7.1 Light attack combo

The basic combo contains four attacks.

Hit| Damage
First hit| 10
Second hit| 12
Third hit| 14
Fourth hit| 18

Initial timing:

- Attack duration: approximately 0.35 seconds.
- Recovery: approximately 0.18 seconds.

The final hit should have stronger knockback.

The player must be able to chain attacks by pressing the attack button at the appropriate time.

If the player waits too long, the combo resets.

7.2 Heavy attack

Initial configuration:

- Damage: 25.
- Duration: approximately 0.70 seconds.
- Recovery: approximately 0.35 seconds.

Heavy attacks must:

- Deal higher damage.
- Have slower startup.
- Have stronger knockback.
- Be useful against armored enemies.
- Create a more noticeable impact effect.

Heavy attacks must not become universally superior to light attacks.

7.3 Aerial attacks

The player can attack while airborne.

Initial aerial attack damage: 12.

Aerial attacks should support:

- Short aerial combos.
- Enemy knockback.
- Air-to-ground transitions.
- Different animations from ground attacks.

7.4 Dash attack

Initial damage: 15.

The Dash Attack should be a special follow-up action, not a replacement for normal movement.

7.5 Hit reactions

Characters must react to attacks.

Include:

- Light hitstun.
- Heavy hitstun.
- Knockback.
- Launching.
- Grounded recovery.
- Guard break.
- Boss stagger.

Bosses must have specific resistance rules so that players cannot permanently stun-lock them.

7.6 Attack cancellation

Allow limited animation cancellation.

Examples:

- Light attack into Dash.
- Certain attacks into Jump.
- Certain attacks into Block.
- Skill attacks into movement after recovery.

Do not allow unrestricted cancellation of every animation.

Combat must reward good timing and positioning.

---

8. PLAYER ATTRIBUTES

The player begins with these base attributes:

Attribute| Base value
Health| 100
Chakra| 100
Stamina| 100
Chakra regeneration| 3 per second
Health regeneration| None

Health does not regenerate automatically by default.

Healing must come from specific items, rewards, abilities, or designated healing rooms.

8.1 Damage categories

Support different damage types:

- Physical.
- Fire.
- Wind.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Water.
- Yin.
- Yang.
- Poison.
- Explosive.
- Special chakra damage.

Enemies may have resistances and weaknesses.

Damage calculations must be consistent and readable.

8.2 Critical hits

Include a critical-hit system.

Critical chance and critical damage can be improved through temporary run upgrades and permanent progression.

Critical hits must have clear visual feedback.

---

9. DIFFICULTY SYSTEM

Provide these difficulty levels:

Difficulty| Enemy health| Enemy damage
Easy| 75%| 70%
Normal| 100%| 100%
Hard| 140%| 130%
Nightmare| 190%| 170%
Legendary| 250%| 220%

Difficulty must affect more than health and damage.

Higher difficulties must also introduce:

- More aggressive enemy behavior.
- Different enemy combinations.
- More dangerous room hazards.
- More complex boss patterns.
- Reduced healing opportunities where appropriate.
- Better rewards.
- Additional elite encounters.

Do not simply multiply enemy health and call that a difficulty system.

---

10. WEAPON SYSTEM

The player can equip two weapons or weapon slots, depending on the selected equipment configuration.

Supported weapon categories:

- Kunai.
- Shuriken.
- Katana.
- Dual Blades.
- Chakra Blade.
- Heavy Sword.
- Staff.
- Other original ninja tools.

Example base weapon values:

Weapon| Damage| Characteristics
Kunai| 10| Fast, short range
Katana| 20| Balanced
Heavy Sword| 35| Slow, powerful
Shuriken| 8| Ranged projectile

These are starting balance values.

Each weapon must have:

- Unique attack animations.
- Unique attack speed.
- Unique range.
- Unique hitboxes.
- Unique sound effects.
- Different strengths and weaknesses.

Weapons must be visually represented on the character when equipped.

Weapons may be improved through rewards and permanent progression.

Do not make every weapon function identically with only different damage numbers.

---

11. ENEMY AI

Enemies must have functional behavior.

They must not simply stand still and repeatedly attack.

Each enemy type should have:

- Detection range.
- Movement behavior.
- Attack range.
- Attack cooldown.
- Defensive behavior.
- Hit reactions.
- Attack telegraphs.
- Death animation.
- Reward configuration.

Enemy archetypes may include:

1. Basic rogue ninja.
2. Melee shinobi.
3. Ranged kunai user.
4. Sword fighter.
5. Fast assassin.
6. Defensive warrior.
7. Chakra caster.
8. Summoner.
9. Poison specialist.
10. Explosive specialist.
11. Elite shinobi.
12. Mini-boss.

Enemies must be able to:

- Approach the player.
- Maintain appropriate attack distance.
- Attack.
- Retreat when appropriate.
- React to blocking and parrying.
- React to knockback.
- Use special abilities.
- Coordinate with other enemies when necessary.

Different enemies must have different attack patterns.

---

12. PIXEL ART AND ANIMATION REQUIREMENTS

Use polished, consistent pixel art.

Visual direction:

- Detailed pixel-art environments.
- Strong silhouettes.
- Readable characters.
- Fluid combat animations.
- Distinct enemy designs.
- Clear attack effects.
- Layered backgrounds.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Controlled particle effects.

Use the Naruto universe as the thematic foundation, but create original game assets rather than copying Dead Cells assets.

Required animation states include:

- Idle.
- Run.
- Jump.
- Fall.
- Land.
- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Aerial attacks.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Hit reaction.
- Knockback.
- Skill activation.
- Death.

Animation must match gameplay timing.

Do not use one generic animation for every attack.

---

13. TECHNICAL QUALITY REQUIREMENTS

Target platform: Android mobile devices.

Performance target: 60 FPS.

The game must:

- Use optimized 2D rendering.
- Avoid unnecessary particle effects.
- Pool frequently created projectiles and effects where possible.
- Avoid excessive memory allocation during combat.
- Keep controls responsive.
- Maintain stable frame pacing.
- Support different landscape screen ratios.
- Save player progression.
- Avoid losing saved data after closing the game.

Do not sacrifice gameplay responsiveness for unnecessary visual effects.

---

14. DEVELOPMENT RULES

The development AI must follow these rules:

1. Do not create the entire game as one rushed implementation.
2. Build and test one system at a time.
3. Do not create fake buttons or nonfunctional menus.
4. Do not leave important mechanics as placeholders.
5. Do not silently remove requirements.
6. Do not replace complex mechanics with generic approximations.
7. Keep systems modular and compatible with future additions.
8. Preserve existing functionality when adding new systems.
9. Test all controls on an actual mobile-sized landscape layout.
10. Prioritize playable functionality over decorative elements.

The first playable prototype must contain:

- Landscape orientation.
- Side-view camera.
- One playable character.
- Horizontal movement.
- Jumping.
- Basic enemy.
- Light attacks.
- Heavy attacks.
- Dash.
- Block.
- Parry.
- Health.
- Chakra.
- Stamina.
- One functional room.

Only after these systems work correctly should the project expand.

END OF PART 1 OF 4.

Continue with Part 2 of this same master document. Do not rewrite, remove, or contradict Part 1.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

# Skill: OpenCode

# OpenCode

Use this guide as the starting point for work involving OpenCode itself. It
covers the core concepts needed to configure and customize OpenCode, extend it
with plugins, and build integrations with the OpenCode SDK, clients, and API.

Full documentation is available at <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/>. This overview is
only an index of core concepts. Before answering a question about a topic below,
fetch the URL named in that section and use the full page as the source of
truth. Follow links from that page when the question needs more detail. Fetch
<https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> first when you need to discover the relevant
documentation page.

A machine-readable documentation index is available at
<https://opencode.ai/v2/llms.txt>.

## Version policy

Always answer for OpenCode V2 unless the user explicitly asks about V1,
legacy OpenCode, or migrating from V1.

Use only <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/> documentation as the source of truth for V2.
Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> accepts both V2 fields and deprecated V1
fields. Never recommend a field it marks deprecated. If V2 documentation is
missing or contradictory, state the uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Config changes apply without a restart. OpenCode watches config files and
reloads agents, commands, skills, MCP servers, and plugins after a save. The TUI
does the same for `cli.json`. To force a full reload, use `/reload`. Don't tell
the user to restart OpenCode after editing config.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. Restart it only if it is stuck or unhealthy, not to apply
configuration changes:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:


MASTER GAME DEVELOPMENT PROMPT

PART 2 OF 4 — CLANS, SPINS, ELEMENTS, BLOODLINES, DOJUTSU, TAIJUTSU, BIJUU AND PROGRESSION


This section continues Part 1 of the same game development project.


Do not restart the project or replace any previously implemented systems. Integrate everything described below into the existing game architecture.


All menus and interfaces described in this section must follow the landscape orientation requirements from Part 1.


---


15. CHARACTER CREATION AND NINJA IDENTITY


Every player must have a customizable ninja character.


Character customization must include:


- Character name.
- Hairstyle.
- Hair color.
- Skin tone options.
- Outfit.
- Headband.
- Accessories.
- Weapon appearance.
- Cosmetic effects.
- Character animations.


The character must visually represent their equipped abilities and equipment.


For example:


- Uchiha characters should have appropriate Sharingan visual effects when activated.
- Hyuga characters should have Byakugan activation effects.
- Bijuu users should display the appropriate chakra aura.
- Eight Gates users should display progressive visual changes when activating the Gates.


Do not make every player look identical.


Customization must be presented in a horizontal interface.


Suggested layout:


- Left: large character preview.
- Center: customization categories.
- Right: selected item details and options.
- Bottom: confirmation and reset controls.


---


16. CLAN SYSTEM


Clans are a permanent part of the player's identity.


Every clan must have:


- Unique passive bonuses.
- Exclusive abilities.
- Unique visual characteristics.
- Different combat advantages.
- Specific progression paths.
- Clan-specific unlocks.


Clan abilities must not be available to players outside their respective clans unless explicitly stated otherwise.


16.1 Required clans


Implement the following clans:


1. Uchiha.
2. Hyuga.
3. Uzumaki.
4. Senju.
5. Kaguya.
6. Nara.
7. Yamanaka.
8. Akimichi.
9. Aburame.
10. Inuzuka.
11. Lee/Guy lineage.


Additional clans may be added later, but these must exist.


16.2 Uchiha Clan


Specialization: Sharingan, visual perception, fire techniques, and powerful offensive abilities.


Passive characteristics:


- Improved combat perception.
- Increased effectiveness with certain fire techniques.
- Bonuses to specific counterattack abilities.


Exclusive abilities may include:


- Fire Style: Great Fireball Technique.
- Fire Style: Phoenix Flower Technique.
- Sharingan activation.
- Sharingan perception abilities.
- Advanced Sharingan techniques.
- Mangekyou-exclusive techniques.


All Sharingan evolutions must remain exclusive to the Uchiha Clan.


A non-Uchiha character must never obtain Sharingan through ordinary spins, rewards, or random drops.


16.3 Hyuga Clan


Specialization: Byakugan, close combat, precision, and chakra-point attacks.


Passive characteristics:


- Improved enemy detection.
- Better precision.
- Bonuses to close-range attacks.


Exclusive abilities:


- Byakugan activation.
- Gentle Fist.
- Eight Trigrams techniques.
- Rotation.
- Vacuum Palm.
- Advanced Hyuga techniques.


Byakugan must remain exclusive to the Hyuga Clan.


16.4 Uzumaki Clan


Specialization: Chakra reserves, vitality, sealing, and endurance.


Passive characteristics:


- Increased maximum chakra.
- Improved chakra-related progression.
- Increased survivability.


Exclusive abilities may include:


- Chakra Chains.
- Sealing techniques.
- Advanced chakra control.
- Special defensive techniques.


16.5 Senju Clan


Specialization: Vitality, balanced combat, and exceptional chakra control.


Passive characteristics:


- Increased health.
- Improved survivability.
- Bonuses to selected elemental techniques.


Exclusive abilities may include:


- Wood Style access where appropriate.
- Advanced vitality techniques.
- Special nature-based abilities.


16.6 Kaguya Clan


Specialization: Bone manipulation and close-range combat.


Exclusive abilities:


- Bone-based attacks.
- Bone armor.
- Bone projectiles.
- Close-range bone combinations.
- Advanced skeletal techniques.


16.7 Nara Clan


Specialization: Shadow manipulation and battlefield control.


Exclusive abilities:


- Shadow Possession.
- Shadow Stitching.
- Shadow-based traps.
- Area control techniques.


16.8 Yamanaka Clan


Specialization: Mind techniques and control.


Exclusive abilities:


- Mind Transfer.
- Mind disruption.
- Special perception abilities.
- Mind-based control techniques.


16.9 Akimichi Clan


Specialization: Physical power and body expansion.


Exclusive abilities:


- Partial Expansion.
- Human Boulder.
- Expansion-based attacks.
- Advanced physical techniques.


16.10 Aburame Clan


Specialization: Insect manipulation.


Exclusive abilities:


- Insect swarms.
- Insect tracking.
- Chakra-draining insects.
- Defensive insect techniques.


16.11 Inuzuka Clan


Specialization: Beast cooperation and tracking.


Exclusive abilities:


- Beast partner.
- Fang Over Fang.
- Dynamic Marking.
- Tracking abilities.
- Combined beast attacks.


16.12 Lee/Guy Lineage


Specialization: Taijutsu, physical training, speed, and the Eight Gates.


This lineage is special.


It must have access to the exclusive Strong Fist fighting style and the Eight Gates progression system.


Exclusive techniques may include:


- Strong Fist.
- Dynamic Entry.
- Front Lotus.
- Primary Lotus.
- Reverse Lotus.
- Advanced physical combinations.
- Eight Gates activation.


Taijutsu specialization and the Eight Gates must be exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not create a universal Taijutsu spin.


Do not allow unrelated clans to randomly obtain Strong Fist or the Eight Gates.


Other characters may use basic physical attacks, but they cannot unlock this specialized fighting style through ordinary progression.


---


17. SPIN SYSTEM


The game must have a spin system for obtaining permanent character traits.


The spin system must be presented through separate categories.


Every new player starts with:


Spin category| Starting spins
Clan Spins| 20
Element Spins| 20
Bloodline Spins| 20
Dojutsu Spins| 20


These are four independent categories.


There must be no Bijuu Spins.


There must be no universal Taijutsu Spins.


The player must be able to use spins from the corresponding category only.


17.1 Clan Spins


Clan Spins determine the player's clan.


The result must permanently unlock the selected clan.


Clan rarity and strength must influence the probability of obtaining specific clans.


Do not make every clan equally likely if some clans are designed to be significantly stronger or rarer.


17.2 Element Spins


Element Spins determine the player's elemental affinity.


Possible results:


- Fire.
- Wind.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Water.
- Yin.
- Yang.


Special advanced elemental combinations may be obtained through the Bloodline system rather than being treated as ordinary base elements.


17.3 Bloodline Spins


Bloodline Spins determine special bloodline abilities.


Possible results include:


- Wood Release.
- Ice Release.
- Lava Release.
- Boil Release.
- Storm Release.
- Magnet Release.
- Explosion Release.
- Scorch Release.
- Dust Release.


Bloodline results must respect clan restrictions where applicable.


A bloodline that requires a specific clan must not be obtainable by an incompatible character.


17.4 Dojutsu Spins


Dojutsu Spins determine ordinary ocular abilities.


Possible results must respect clan exclusivity.


Examples:


- Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Mangekyou Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Byakugan: Hyuga only.


All evolutions of the Sharingan remain Uchiha-exclusive.


Byakugan remains Hyuga-exclusive.


Other clan-exclusive ocular abilities must follow their respective restrictions.


Rinnegan is the only independent exception.


It is not obtained through Dojutsu Spins.


Its acquisition rules are described in Section 20.


17.5 Spin rarity system


Use these initial rarity probabilities:


Rarity| Probability
Common| 50%
Uncommon| 25%
Rare| 15%
Epic| 7%
Legendary| 2.5%
Mythical| 0.5%


The rarity system must influence the results within each applicable spin category.


Do not use one universal result table for all categories.


Each category must have its own compatible result pool.


17.6 Spin animation


The spin interface must be horizontal.


Suggested layout:


- Left: category name and current spin count.
- Center: large animated result display.
- Right: selected result information.
- Bottom: Spin x1, Spin x10, and Auto Spin controls where available.


Animation requirements:


- Clear rolling animation.
- Rarity-based visual effects.
- Distinct sound effects.
- Special reveal animation for Legendary and Mythical results.
- Skip animation option.


The animation must not interfere with the actual random result.


17.7 Duplicate results


If the player receives a duplicate result:


- Convert it into an appropriate compensation currency.
- Display the duplicate clearly.
- Show the amount of compensation received.
- Allow the player to use that currency in designated progression systems.


Do not silently discard duplicate results.


17.8 Permanent unlocks


Spin results must be saved permanently.


Closing the game must not reset obtained clans, elements, bloodlines, or dojutsu.


---


18. ELEMENTAL SYSTEM


Every elemental affinity must have its own abilities and combat identity.


The initial elemental categories are:


- Fire.
- Wind.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Water.
- Yin.
- Yang.


Each element must have at least five functional abilities.


Each ability must have:


- Name.
- Description.
- Damage.
- Chakra cost.
- Cooldown.
- Range.
- Startup time.
- Active duration.
- Recovery time.
- Hitbox.
- Animation.
- Visual effects.
- Upgrade path.


Do not create abilities that only have different names and identical effects.


18.1 Fire Release


Focus: damage, area control, and burning.


Example abilities:


1. Fireball Technique.
2. Phoenix Flower Technique.
3. Great Fireball Technique.
4. Flame Wall.
5. Dragon Flame Technique.


Reference values:


Ability| Damage| Chakra| Cooldown
Fireball| 25| 15| 4 s
Phoenix Flower| 8 per projectile| 20| 6 s
Great Fireball| 45| 35| 10 s


18.2 Wind Release


Focus: range, slicing attacks, and knockback.


Example abilities:


1. Wind Blade.
2. Vacuum Wave.
3. Wind Bullet.
4. Gale Burst.
5. Great Wind Cutter.


18.3 Lightning Release


Focus: speed, piercing damage, and electrical effects.


Example abilities:


1. Lightning Blade.
2. Chidori.
3. Lightning Field.
4. Lightning Projectile.
5. Thunder Burst.


Reference values:


Ability| Damage| Chakra| Cooldown
Lightning Blade| 45| 30| 8 s
Chidori| 55| 35| 9 s


18.4 Earth Release


Focus: defense, terrain control, and heavy attacks.


Example abilities:


1. Earth Wall.
2. Earth Spear.
3. Earth Dragon.
4. Ground Spike.
5. Earth Prison.


18.5 Water Release


Focus: ranged attacks, control, and continuous pressure.


Example abilities:


1. Water Bullet.
2. Water Dragon.
3. Water Prison.
4. Water Wave.
5. Water Shark Projectile.


18.6 Yin Release


Focus: perception, illusion-like effects, and specialized chakra techniques.


18.7 Yang Release


Focus: vitality, physical enhancement, and support techniques.


18.8 Advanced elemental combinations


Include these bloodline-based elemental combinations:


- Wood Release.
- Ice Release.
- Lava Release.
- Boil Release.
- Storm Release.
- Magnet Release.
- Explosion Release.
- Scorch Release.
- Dust Release.


These must be implemented as distinct abilities with their own visual effects and mechanics.


Do not make advanced combinations available to every character automatically.


---


19. DOJUTSU SYSTEM


Dojutsu abilities must have meaningful combat effects.


They must not be simple cosmetic eye changes.


19.1 Sharingan progression


Sharingan is exclusive to Uchiha.


Progression:


1. Sharingan.
2. Three-Tomoe Sharingan.
3. Mangekyou Sharingan.
4. Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.


Each evolution must improve the character's abilities.


Possible effects:


- Improved attack perception.
- Better enemy telegraph recognition.
- Special counterattack opportunities.
- Improved reaction abilities.
- Access to unique Uchiha techniques.
- Advanced ocular abilities.


Mangekyou abilities must have appropriate cooldowns and chakra costs.


19.2 Byakugan progression


Byakugan is exclusive to Hyuga.


Possible effects:


- Expanded enemy detection.
- Better perception of incoming attacks.
- Improved precision.
- Access to advanced Gentle Fist techniques.
- Enhanced battlefield awareness.


19.3 Other ocular abilities


Additional clan-exclusive dojutsu may be added.


Every ocular ability must have explicit ownership restrictions.


Do not allow an ordinary random spin to bypass clan restrictions.


19.4 Rinnegan — independent special reward


Rinnegan is the only independent exception to the clan-exclusive dojutsu rules.


It can be obtained by any player, regardless of clan.


However:


- It cannot be obtained through Dojutsu Spins.
- It cannot be obtained through Clan Spins.
- It cannot be obtained through ordinary random item drops.
- It must not replace ordinary reward choices.
- It must not be confused with Bijuu cards.


After clearing an eligible room, there is exactly a 0.5% chance for Rinnegan to appear as a special additional reward choice.


This is a separate special reward roll.


It must not remove or replace the room's normal reward slots.


When successfully obtained:


- Permanently unlock Rinnegan.
- Save the unlock.
- Display a unique reveal animation.
- Provide a special notification.
- Allow the player to equip it through the appropriate character progression interface.


Rinnegan must be extremely rare.


The 0.5% probability must be applied exactly as specified.


---


20. BIJUU SYSTEM


The Bijuu system is one of the game's most important special progression systems.


There are nine Bijuu:


1. Shukaku.
2. Matatabi.
3. Isobu.
4. Son Goku.
5. Kokuo.
6. Saiken.
7. Chomei.
8. Gyuki.
9. Kurama.


Bijuu are NOT obtained through spins.


Do not create a Bijuu Spin category.


Do not put Bijuu inside the ordinary Clan, Element, Bloodline, or Dojutsu spin pools.


20.1 Bijuu acquisition


Each Bijuu must have its own special super-boss encounter.


The player must:


1. Discover or unlock the corresponding Bijuu challenge.
2. Enter its dedicated arena.
3. Fight the Bijuu.
4. Survive its unique attack patterns.
5. Defeat it.
6. Receive its Bijuu Card as a reward.


Each Bijuu encounter must be extremely difficult.


These are optional super-boss encounters, not ordinary mandatory story bosses.


The player must not automatically receive a Bijuu simply by progressing through the main story.


20.2 Bijuu boss design


Every Bijuu must have:


- Dedicated arena.
- Unique background.
- Unique music.
- Unique entrance animation.
- Unique attack patterns.
- Multiple combat phases.
- Distinctive visual effects.
- Large health bar.
- Special defeat animation.
- Bijuu Card reward.


Bijuu must feel significantly more dangerous than normal bosses.


Their attacks should require movement, positioning, blocking, parrying where appropriate, and precise dodging.


20.3 Bijuu Cards


Each defeated Bijuu grants its corresponding card.


The card permanently unlocks the ability to use that Bijuu's power.


Cards must be visible in the player's collection.


Each card must contain:


- Bijuu name.
- Bijuu artwork.
- Description.
- Associated abilities.
- Transformation options.
- Unlock status.


20.4 Equipping Bijuu


The player may equip one primary Bijuu at a time.


Changing the equipped Bijuu must happen through an appropriate menu or designated safe location.


Do not allow the player to equip all nine simultaneously.


20.5 Bijuu abilities and transformations


Bijuu progression may include:


1. Chakra cloak.
2. Partial transformation.
3. Advanced transformation.
4. Full transformation.


These stages must have different visual effects and gameplay consequences.


Transformations may modify:


- Character sprite.
- Aura.
- Attack animations.
- Movement.
- Damage.
- Defense.
- Available abilities.
- Chakra consumption.


Transformations must consume chakra and must not remain active indefinitely without a cost.


Each Bijuu must have abilities inspired by its individual identity.


Do not make all nine Bijuu transformations identical with different colors.


---


21. TAIJUTSU AND EIGHT GATES


The specialized Taijutsu system belongs exclusively to the Lee/Guy lineage.


There must be no universal Taijutsu spin.


Characters outside this lineage can still use basic melee attacks, but they cannot unlock Strong Fist or the Eight Gates.


21.1 Strong Fist


Strong Fist is the main specialized fighting style.


It must have:


- Unique attack animations.
- Fast combinations.
- Powerful physical attacks.
- High mobility.
- Strong knockback.
- Special aerial attacks.


21.2 Exclusive techniques


Implement:


- Dynamic Entry.
- Front Lotus.
- Primary Lotus.
- Reverse Lotus.
- Advanced Strong Fist combinations.


These abilities must be unlocked progressively.


21.3 Eight Gates progression


Implement the Eight Gates as a progressive power system.


Each Gate must increase power while introducing meaningful costs and limitations.


The player must unlock the Gates progressively rather than receiving all of them immediately.


The Gates should change:


- Character aura.
- Character animation.
- Movement speed.
- Attack speed.
- Damage.
- Special attack availability.
- Chakra or stamina consumption.
- Visual effects.


Higher Gates must be significantly stronger and more demanding to use.


Do not make the Eight Gates a permanent passive bonus.


They are temporary combat transformations with meaningful activation and resource costs.


---


22. PERMANENT AND TEMPORARY PROGRESSION


The game must have two separate progression layers.


22.1 Permanent progression


These unlocks remain after death:


- Clan.
- Elemental affinity.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Rinnegan unlock.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Taijutsu lineage progression.
- Permanent equipment unlocks.
- Character customization.
- Achievements.
- Story progress.
- Permanent abilities.
- Permanent upgrades.


22.2 Temporary run progression


These bonuses exist only during the current run.


Examples:


- Increased damage.
- Increased maximum health.
- Increased chakra.
- Increased stamina.
- Critical chance.
- Critical damage.
- Movement speed.
- Attack speed.
- Cooldown reduction.
- Temporary weapons.
- Temporary abilities.
- Temporary defensive bonuses.


When the player dies, temporary run bonuses must reset.


Permanent unlocks must remain.


22.3 Upgrade selection


After eligible encounters, allow the player to choose between multiple upgrades.


Present three reward cards horizontally.


Each card must clearly display:


- Name.
- Icon.
- Rarity.
- Effect.
- Duration or permanence.
- Relevant numerical bonuses.


The player must understand what an upgrade does before selecting it.


22.4 Build diversity


The game must encourage different combinations.


Examples:


- Fast Uchiha fire build.
- Hyuga precision melee build.
- Uzumaki chakra-focused build.
- Lee/Guy physical combat build.
- Ice-based control build.
- Lightning-based burst-damage build.
- Bijuu transformation build.


No single build should automatically dominate every situation.


---


23. PROGRESSION INTERFACE


Create a dedicated progression interface.


It must contain:


- Clan information.
- Element information.
- Bloodline information.
- Dojutsu information.
- Bijuu collection.
- Taijutsu progression.
- Permanent unlocks.
- Equipped abilities.


The layout must be horizontal.


Suggested structure:


- Left: character preview.
- Center: progression categories.
- Right: selected category details.
- Bottom: equip, unlock, and upgrade controls.


Show unavailable abilities with clear requirements.


Do not display locked abilities as if they were already usable.


---


24. DATA AND SAVE REQUIREMENTS


Every permanent unlock must be saved reliably.


Save:


- Player identity.
- Clan.
- Element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Rinnegan unlock.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Equipped Bijuu.
- Taijutsu progression.
- Permanent equipment.
- Spin counts.
- Obtained results.
- Currency.
- Achievements.
- Story progress.
- Settings.
- Control customization.


Do not reset permanent progression when starting a new run.


Do not reset saved progression when closing the game.


The spin system must not grant an item without recording the result.


Bijuu Cards must only be granted after the corresponding super-boss has actually been defeated.


Rinnegan must only be granted through its special 0.5% reward roll.


---


25. DEVELOPMENT VALIDATION FOR PART 2


Before moving on to the next major development phase, verify the following:


1. Every required clan exists.
2. Clan passives work.
3. Clan-exclusive abilities respect restrictions.
4. New players receive exactly 20 spins in each of the four categories.
5. There is no Bijuu Spin.
6. There is no universal Taijutsu Spin.
7. Sharingan is Uchiha-exclusive.
8. Byakugan is Hyuga-exclusive.
9. Sharingan evolutions are Uchiha-exclusive.
10. Rinnegan is not obtainable through spins.
11. Rinnegan has exactly a 0.5% special reward chance after eligible room clears.
12. Rinnegan does not replace ordinary rewards.
13. All nine Bijuu have separate super-boss encounters.
14. Each Bijuu grants its own card after defeat.
15. Only one primary Bijuu can be equipped at a time.
16. Strong Fist and Eight Gates are exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
17. Permanent progression survives death.
18. Temporary run upgrades reset after death.
19. The progression interface is landscape.
20. All menus remain compatible with the landscape layout.


Do not proceed if these restrictions are being ignored.


END OF PART 2 OF 4.


Continue with Part 3 of the same master document. Preserve all previous systems and restrictions.

It must have access to the exclusive Strong Fist fighting style and the Eight Gates progression system.


Exclusive techniques may include:


- Strong Fist.
- Dynamic Entry.
- Front Lotus.
- Primary Lotus.
- Reverse Lotus.
- Advanced physical combinations.
- Eight Gates activation.


Taijutsu specialization and the Eight Gates must be exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.


Do not create a universal Taijutsu spin.


Do not allow unrelated clans to randomly obtain Strong Fist or the Eight Gates.


Other characters may use basic physical attacks, but they cannot unlock this specialized fighting style through ordinary progression.


---


17. SPIN SYSTEM


The game must have a spin system for obtaining permanent character traits.


The spin system must be presented through separate categories.


Every new player starts with:


Spin category| Starting spins
Clan Spins| 20
Element Spins| 20
Bloodline Spins| 20
Dojutsu Spins| 20


These are four independent categories.


There must be no Bijuu Spins.


There must be no universal Taijutsu Spins.


The player must be able to use spins from the corresponding category only.


17.1 Clan Spins


Clan Spins determine the player's clan.


The result must permanently unlock the selected clan.


Clan rarity and strength must influence the probability of obtaining specific clans.


Do not make every clan equally likely if some clans are designed to be significantly stronger or rarer.


17.2 Element Spins


Element Spins determine the player's elemental affinity.


Possible results:


- Fire.
- Wind.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Water.
- Yin.
- Yang.


Special advanced elemental combinations may be obtained through the Bloodline system rather than being treated as ordinary base elements.


17.3 Bloodline Spins


Bloodline Spins determine special bloodline abilities.


Possible results include:


- Wood Release.
- Ice Release.
- Lava Release.
- Boil Release.
- Storm Release.
- Magnet Release.
- Explosion Release.
- Scorch Release.
- Dust Release.


Bloodline results must respect clan restrictions where applicable.


A bloodline that requires a specific clan must not be obtainable by an incompatible character.


17.4 Dojutsu Spins


Dojutsu Spins determine ordinary ocular abilities.


Possible results must respect clan exclusivity.


Examples:


- Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Three-Tomoe Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Mangekyou Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan: Uchiha only.
- Byakugan: Hyuga only.


All evolutions of the Sharingan remain Uchiha-exclusive.


Byakugan remains Hyuga-exclusive.


Other clan-exclusive ocular abilities must follow their respective restrictions.


Rinnegan is the only independent exception.


It is not obtained through Dojutsu Spins.


Its acquisition rules are described in Section 20.


17.5 Spin rarity system


Use these initial rarity probabilities:


Rarity| Probability
Common| 50%
Uncommon| 25%
Rare| 15%
Epic| 7%
Legendary| 2.5%
Mythical| 0.5%


The rarity system must influence the results within each applicable spin category.


Do not use one universal result table for all categories.


Each category must have its own compatible result pool.


17.6 Spin animation


The spin interface must be horizontal.


Suggested layout:


- Left: category name and current spin count.
- Center: large animated result display.
- Right: selected result information.
- Bottom: Spin x1, Spin x10, and Auto Spin controls where available.


Animation requirements:


- Clear rolling animation.
- Rarity-based visual effects.
- Distinct sound effects.
- Special reveal animation for Legendary and Mythical results.
- Skip animation option.


The animation must not interfere with the actual random result.


17.7 Duplicate results


If the player receives a duplicate result:


- Convert it into an appropriate compensation currency.
- Display the duplicate clearly.
- Show the amount of compensation received.
- Allow the player to use that currency in designated progression systems.


Do not silently discard duplicate results.


17.8 Permanent unlocks


Spin results must be saved permanently.


Closing the game must not reset obtained clans, elements, bloodlines, or dojutsu.


---


18. ELEMENTAL SYSTEM


Every elemental affinity must have its own abilities and combat identity.


The initial elemental categories are:


- Fire.
- Wind.
- Lightning.
- Earth.
- Water.
- Yin.
- Yang.


Each element must have at least five functional abilities.


Each ability must have:


- Name.
- Description.
- Damage.
- Chakra cost.
- Cooldown.
- Range.
- Startup time.
- Active duration.
- Recovery time.
- Hitbox.
- Animation.
- Visual effects.
- Upgrade path.


Do not create abilities that only have different names and identical effects.


18.1 Fire Release


Focus: damage, area control, and burning.


Example abilities:


1. Fireball Technique.
2. Phoenix Flower Technique.
3. Great Fireball Technique.
4. Flame Wall.
5. Dragon Flame Technique.


Reference values:


Ability| Damage| Chakra| Cooldown
Fireball| 25| 15| 4 s
Phoenix Flower| 8 per projectile| 20| 6 s
Great Fireball| 45| 35| 10 s


18.2 Wind Release


Focus: range, slicing attacks, and knockback.


Example abilities:


1. Wind Blade.
2. Vacuum Wave.
3. Wind Bullet.
4. Gale Burst.
5. Great Wind Cutter.


18.3 Lightning Release


Focus: speed, piercing damage, and electrical effects.


Example abilities:


1. Lightning Blade.
2. Chidori.
3. Lightning Field.
4. Lightning Projectile.
5. Thunder Burst.


Reference values:


Ability| Damage| Chakra| Cooldown
Lightning Blade| 45| 30| 8 s
Chidori| 55| 35| 9 s


18.4 Earth Release


Focus: defense, terrain control, and heavy attacks.


Example abilities:


1. Earth Wall.
2. Earth Spear.
3. Earth Dragon.
4. Ground Spike.
5. Earth Prison.


18.5 Water Release


Focus: ranged attacks, control, and continuous pressure.


Example abilities:


1. Water Bullet.
2. Water Dragon.
3. Water Prison.
4. Water Wave.
5. Water Shark Projectile.


18.6 Yin Release


Focus: perception, illusion-like effects, and specialized chakra techniques.


18.7 Yang Release


Focus: vitality, physical enhancement, and support techniques.


18.8 Advanced elemental combinations


Include these bloodline-based elemental combinations:


- Wood Release.
- Ice Release.
- Lava Release.
- Boil Release.
- Storm Release.
- Magnet Release.
- Explosion Release.
- Scorch Release.
- Dust Release.


These must be implemented as distinct abilities with their own visual effects and mechanics.


Do not make advanced combinations available to every character automatically.


---


19. DOJUTSU SYSTEM


Dojutsu abilities must have meaningful combat effects.


They must not be simple cosmetic eye changes.


19.1 Sharingan progression


Sharingan is exclusive to Uchiha.


Progression:


1. Sharingan.
2. Three-Tomoe Sharingan.
3. Mangekyou Sharingan.
4. Eternal Mangekyou Sharingan.


Each evolution must improve the character's abilities.


Possible effects:


- Improved attack perception.
- Better enemy telegraph recognition.
- Special counterattack opportunities.
- Improved reaction abilities.
- Access to unique Uchiha techniques.
- Advanced ocular abilities.


Mangekyou abilities must have appropriate cooldowns and chakra costs.


19.2 Byakugan progression


Byakugan is exclusive to Hyuga.


Possible effects:


- Expanded enemy detection.
- Better perception of incoming attacks.
- Improved precision.
- Access to advanced Gentle Fist techniques.
- Enhanced battlefield awareness.


19.3 Other ocular abilities


Additional clan-exclusive dojutsu may be added.


Every ocular ability must have explicit ownership restrictions.


Do not allow an ordinary random spin to bypass clan restrictions.


19.4 Rinnegan — independent special reward


Rinnegan is the only independent exception to the clan-exclusive dojutsu rules.


It can be obtained by any player, regardless of clan.


However:


- It cannot be obtained through Dojutsu Spins.
- It cannot be obtained through Clan Spins.
- It cannot be obtained through ordinary random item drops.
- It must not replace ordinary reward choices.
- It must not be confused with Bijuu cards.


After clearing an eligible room, there is exactly a 0.5% chance for Rinnegan to appear as a special additional reward choice.


This is a separate special reward roll.


It must not remove or replace the room's normal reward slots.


When successfully obtained:


- Permanently unlock Rinnegan.
- Save the unlock.
- Display a unique reveal animation.
- Provide a special notification.
- Allow the player to equip it through the appropriate character progression interface.


Rinnegan must be extremely rare.


The 0.5% probability must be applied exactly as specified.


---


20. BIJUU SYSTEM


The Bijuu system is one of the game's most important special progression systems.


There are nine Bijuu:


1. Shukaku.
2. Matatabi.
3. Isobu.
4. Son Goku.
5. Kokuo.
6. Saiken.
7. Chomei.
8. Gyuki.
9. Kurama.


Bijuu are NOT obtained through spins.


Do not create a Bijuu Spin category.


Do not put Bijuu inside the ordinary Clan, Element, Bloodline, or Dojutsu spin pools.


20.1 Bijuu acquisition


Each Bijuu must have its own special super-boss encounter.


The player must:


1. Discover or unlock the corresponding Bijuu challenge.
2. Enter its dedicated arena.
3. Fight the Bijuu.
4. Survive its unique attack patterns.
5. Defeat it.
6. Receive its Bijuu Card as a reward.


Each Bijuu encounter must be extremely difficult.


These are optional super-boss encounters, not ordinary mandatory story bosses.


The player must not automatically receive a Bijuu simply by progressing through the main story.


20.2 Bijuu boss design


Every Bijuu must have:


- Dedicated arena.
- Unique background.
- Unique music.
- Unique entrance animation.
- Unique attack patterns.
- Multiple combat phases.
- Distinctive visual effects.
- Large health bar.
- Special defeat animation.
- Bijuu Card reward.


Bijuu must feel significantly more dangerous than normal bosses.


Their attacks should require movement, positioning, blocking, parrying where appropriate, and precise dodging.


20.3 Bijuu Cards


Each defeated Bijuu grants its corresponding card.


The card permanently unlocks the ability to use that Bijuu's power.


Cards must be visible in the player's collection.


Each card must contain:


- Bijuu name.
- Bijuu artwork.
- Description.
- Associated abilities.
- Transformation options.
- Unlock status.


20.4 Equipping Bijuu


The player may equip one primary Bijuu at a time.


Changing the equipped Bijuu must happen through an appropriate menu or designated safe location.


Do not allow the player to equip all nine simultaneously.


20.5 Bijuu abilities and transformations


Bijuu progression may include:


1. Chakra cloak.
2. Partial transformation.
3. Advanced transformation.
4. Full transformation.


These stages must have different visual effects and gameplay consequences.


Transformations may modify:


- Character sprite.
- Aura.
- Attack animations.
- Movement.
- Damage.
- Defense.
- Available abilities.
- Chakra consumption.


Transformations must consume chakra and must not remain active indefinitely without a cost.


Each Bijuu must have abilities inspired by its individual identity.


Do not make all nine Bijuu transformations identical with different colors.


---


21. TAIJUTSU AND EIGHT GATES


The specialized Taijutsu system belongs exclusively to the Lee/Guy lineage.


There must be no universal Taijutsu spin.


Characters outside this lineage can still use basic melee attacks, but they cannot unlock Strong Fist or the Eight Gates.


21.1 Strong Fist


Strong Fist is the main specialized fighting style.


It must have:


- Unique attack animations.
- Fast combinations.
- Powerful physical attacks.
- High mobility.
- Strong knockback.
- Special aerial attacks.


21.2 Exclusive techniques


Implement:


- Dynamic Entry.
- Front Lotus.
- Primary Lotus.
- Reverse Lotus.
- Advanced Strong Fist combinations.


These abilities must be unlocked progressively.


21.3 Eight Gates progression


Implement the Eight Gates as a progressive power system.


Each Gate must increase power while introducing meaningful costs and limitations.


The player must unlock the Gates progressively rather than receiving all of them immediately.


The Gates should change:


- Character aura.
- Character animation.
- Movement speed.
- Attack speed.
- Damage.
- Special attack availability.
- Chakra or stamina consumption.
- Visual effects.


Higher Gates must be significantly stronger and more demanding to use.


Do not make the Eight Gates a permanent passive bonus.


They are temporary combat transformations with meaningful activation and resource costs.


---


22. PERMANENT AND TEMPORARY PROGRESSION


The game must have two separate progression layers.


22.1 Permanent progression


These unlocks remain after death:


- Clan.
- Elemental affinity.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Rinnegan unlock.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Taijutsu lineage progression.
- Permanent equipment unlocks.
- Character customization.
- Achievements.
- Story progress.
- Permanent abilities.
- Permanent upgrades.


22.2 Temporary run progression


These bonuses exist only during the current run.


Examples:


- Increased damage.
- Increased maximum health.
- Increased chakra.
- Increased stamina.
- Critical chance.
- Critical damage.
- Movement speed.
- Attack speed.
- Cooldown reduction.
- Temporary weapons.
- Temporary abilities.
- Temporary defensive bonuses.


When the player dies, temporary run bonuses must reset.


Permanent unlocks must remain.


22.3 Upgrade selection


After eligible encounters, allow the player to choose between multiple upgrades.


Present three reward cards horizontally.


Each card must clearly display:


- Name.
- Icon.
- Rarity.
- Effect.
- Duration or permanence.
- Relevant numerical bonuses.


The player must understand what an upgrade does before selecting it.


22.4 Build diversity


The game must encourage different combinations.


Examples:


- Fast Uchiha fire build.
- Hyuga precision melee build.
- Uzumaki chakra-focused build.
- Lee/Guy physical combat build.
- Ice-based control build.
- Lightning-based burst-damage build.
- Bijuu transformation build.


No single build should automatically dominate every situation.


---


23. PROGRESSION INTERFACE


Create a dedicated progression interface.


It must contain:


- Clan information.
- Element information.
- Bloodline information.
- Dojutsu information.
- Bijuu collection.
- Taijutsu progression.
- Permanent unlocks.
- Equipped abilities.


The layout must be horizontal.


Suggested structure:


- Left: character preview.
- Center: progression categories.
- Right: selected category details.
- Bottom: equip, unlock, and upgrade controls.


Show unavailable abilities with clear requirements.


Do not display locked abilities as if they were already usable.


---


24. DATA AND SAVE REQUIREMENTS


Every permanent unlock must be saved reliably.


Save:


- Player identity.
- Clan.
- Element.
- Bloodline.
- Dojutsu.
- Rinnegan unlock.
- Bijuu Cards.
- Equipped Bijuu.
- Taijutsu progression.
- Permanent equipment.
- Spin counts.
- Obtained results.
- Currency.
- Achievements.
- Story progress.
- Settings.
- Control customization.


Do not reset permanent progression when starting a new run.


Do not reset saved progression when closing the game.


The spin system must not grant an item without recording the result.


Bijuu Cards must only be granted after the corresponding super-boss has actually been defeated.


Rinnegan must only be granted through its special 0.5% reward roll.


---


25. DEVELOPMENT VALIDATION FOR PART 2


Before moving on to the next major development phase, verify the following:


1. Every required clan exists.
2. Clan passives work.
3. Clan-exclusive abilities respect restrictions.
4. New players receive exactly 20 spins in each of the four categories.
5. There is no Bijuu Spin.
6. There is no universal Taijutsu Spin.
7. Sharingan is Uchiha-exclusive.
8. Byakugan is Hyuga-exclusive.
9. Sharingan evolutions are Uchiha-exclusive.
10. Rinnegan is not obtainable through spins.
11. Rinnegan has exactly a 0.5% special reward chance after eligible room clears.
12. Rinnegan does not replace ordinary rewards.
13. All nine Bijuu have separate super-boss encounters.
14. Each Bijuu grants its own card after defeat.
15. Only one primary Bijuu can be equipped at a time.
16. Strong Fist and Eight Gates are exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
17. Permanent progression survives death.
18. Temporary run upgrades reset after death.
19. The progression interface is landscape.
20. All menus remain compatible with the landscape layout.


Do not proceed if these restrictions are being ignored.


END OF PART 2 OF 4.


Continue with Part 3 of the same master document. Preserve all previous systems and restrictions.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D side-scrolling action roguelike for mobile, inspired by a Naruto-themed ninja action setting, as a first playable prototype with room-based combat and progression.

## Requirements
- Enforce horizontal 16:9 landscape gameplay across gameplay and menus.
- Implement responsive movement, jumping, light/heavy attacks, dash, block/parry, health, chakra, stamina, touch controls, enemy AI, pixel-art presentation, and save persistence.
- The first prototype must include one playable character, basic enemy, functional room, side-view camera, and core combat systems.

## Decisions
- Use an HTML/CSS/Canvas implementation for broad mobile browser compatibility.
- Internal canvas resolution is 960 × 540, with wider landscape layouts filled horizontally.
- Assume a horizontal Naruto-inspired game shell rather than asking for clarifying requirements.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with the game shell, title/menu, modal area, HUD-adjacent touch controls, and pause button.
- Created `style.css` with a landscape 16:9 layout, responsive wider-screen support, coarse-pointer touch controls, and portrait blocking.
- Created an initial `game.js` scaffold containing the canvas, menu state, player/enemy data structures, save loading/persistence, wave setup, and basic enemy archetypes.
- Added project placeholder framework for the action roguelike prototype.

### Active
- The JavaScript gameplay implementation is incomplete; `game.js` ends at an explicit `//__PART2__` placeholder.

### Blocked
- The prototype cannot be considered playable until the main loop, physics, combat, AI, rendering, HUD, touch inputs, and transitions are implemented.

## Next Move
1. Complete `game.js` with keyboard/touch input handling and the fixed-frame game loop.
2. Implement player movement, jumping, dash, attacks, block/parry, enemy AI, damage, and hit reactions.
3. Implement canvas rendering, HUD, room boundaries, particles, projectiles, wave transitions, rewards, pause/menu behavior, and defeat/restart flow.
4. Launch the project locally and verify it at a mobile-sized landscape viewport.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main game HTML and touch-control markup.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Main incomplete gameplay implementation.

- `game.js` is intentionally only partially implemented and ends at `//__PART2__`.
- Existing save keys and save data use `ashesSave`; it includes permanent shards, rank, damage, health, and control settings.
- The prototype currently defines player and enemy state, but no update/render loop or event handlers are present yet.

## Objective
- Build and continue the complete playable HTML/Canvas 2D shinobi action roguelike, preserving its Part 2 progression systems and completing further master-game phases.

## Requirements
- Maintain a 16:9 landscape shell with a `960 × 540` internal canvas.
- Keep keyboard and mobile touch controls, fixed-step combat, room AI, resources, rewards, progression, and persistent saves.
- Preserve `ashesSave` as the save key and permanent-versus-temporary progression behavior.
- Keep clan, spin, element, bloodline, dojutsu, Rinnegan, Bijuu, and Lee/Guy lineage restrictions intact.

## Decisions
- Continue using the existing HTML/CSS/Canvas architecture rather than replacing it.
- Rinnegan remains separate from normal reward choices and rolls exactly 0.5% after eligible room clears.
- Bijuu are not obtainable through spins and require dedicated boss-defeat or challenge logic.
- Strong Fist and Eight Gates remain exclusive to the Lee/Guy lineage.
- Permanent rewards and unlocks persist; temporary run upgrades reset on death.

- Implemented the title, 16:9 shell, HUD, progression modal, controls, touch controls, and mobile portrait handling.
- Implemented movement, jumping, attacks, dash, guard/parry, stamina, chakra, enemy AI, projectiles, particles, and wave combat.

- Implemented nine Bijuu cards, one equipped primary Bijuu, boss arena setup, collection UI, and Bijuu challenge entry.
- Implemented Lee/Guy lineage and Eight Gates availability.
- Implemented permanent identity/progression saves, room rewards, permanent damage/health gains, run chakra restoration, defeat/victory, and restart flows.
- Implemented independent Rinnegan reveal handling and passed `node --check game.js`.

- Continue Part 3 and any remaining master-game progression work.
- Validate gameplay and progression behavior through local mobile-sized landscape browser testing.
